am.nc.0001.summary: The two axes you're linking with an electronic cam must belong to the same logical machine.
likely_causes: The cam axes are attached to different logical machines
resolution_steps: Check which logical machine each of the two axes is attached to.
Either update the database so both axes belong to the same logical machine, or transfer one axis at run time so both share a logical machine before enabling the cam.
Re-enable the electronic cam once both axes are on the same logical machine.
am.nc.0001.notes: Scenario and fix provided by engineering (AMCore Core Alarm Design page); confirm exact section anchors during build.

am.nc.0002.summary: An axis can only be attached to one logical machine at a time; it must be released before it can be attached elsewhere.
likely_causes: The axis was not released from its current logical machine before ATTACH
resolution_steps: Release the axis from its current logical machine before attaching it to another.
Coordinate the transfer using DETACH, BARRIER and ATTACH in the correct order.
Use a BARRIER to synchronise the logical machines so the axis is free at the point of ATTACH.
am.nc.0002.notes: Scenario and fix provided by engineering.

am.nc.0003.summary: The M-code is set to run an EPPL part program, but that program file can't be found.
likely_causes: M-code configured as mode 4 (EPPL) but the part program is missing
M-code should be handled by PLC but is configured as mode 4
resolution_steps: Decide whether M101 should be implemented in PLC or as an EPPL part program.
If PLC: configure the M-code to a PLC mode (1–3 or 5–7), e.g. mcode.101.mode = 5.
If EPPL: place m101.pp in one of the folders on the part program search hierarchy.
Confirm the search hierarchy includes that folder.

doc_refs.section: Define a part program search hierarchy

am.nc.0003.notes: Scenario and fix provided by engineering; both mode configuration and search hierarchy are documented.

am.nc.0004.summary: A spline needs at least three control points between splineon and splineoff.
likely_causes: Confusing start/end points with control points
resolution_steps: Ensure there are at least 3 control points between splineon and splineoff.
Distinguish control points from the start/end points.
Add control points as needed and re-run.
am.nc.0004.notes: Scenario and fix provided by engineering; ANCA Mate can explain control vs dummy points from the docs.

am.nc.0005.summary: A single program block may contain only one class 1 preparatory word.
likely_causes: Two or more class 1 preparatory words placed in one block
resolution_steps: Identify the class 1 preparatory words in the block (see the class 1 list in the preparatory-word reference).
Split them across separate blocks so each block has at most one class 1 word.
Re-run the program.
am.nc.0005.notes: Value-add: the docs contain the list of class 1 words, which isn't obvious from the message.

am.cfg.0001.summary: Two joints are configured to use the same device (logical address); each must be unique.
likely_causes: Duplicate device address across two joints in the configuration
resolution_steps: Find the joints/axes that share the same device (logical address).
Reconfigure one of them to use a different device address.
Restart AMCore and confirm startup completes without the assertion.
am.cfg.0001.notes: Scenario and fix provided by engineering; ANCA Mate can explain the device/joint parameters.

am.lic.0001.summary: The OPC UA server is enabled but your license doesn't include it; either disable it or purchase the option.
likely_causes: opcua.enable = true without a license that includes the OPC UA option
resolution_steps: If you don't need the OPC UA server, set the configuration property opcua.enable = false.
If you do need it, contact ANCA to add the OPC UA option to your license.
am.lic.0001.notes: Deliberately chosen so the documented fix is the configuration property (opcua.enable); changing the license itself is out of scope of the supplied docs.

am.fb.0001.summary: A device dropped out of the operational state; the machine has stopped.
likely_causes: A device fell out of the OP state
A drive fault forced a state change
resolution_steps: Note the device name and station address in the message.
Restart the system to re-initialise the EtherCAT bus.
If the same device drops out again, restart (power-cycle) that drive specifically.
am.fb.0001.notes: Resolution is verbatim doc guidance: 'Almost always requires a system restart, and in some cases, a drive restart.' Source doc is DRAFT.

am.fb.0002.summary: A drive raised an emergency and is stuck in an error state.
likely_causes: Drive-reported fault (over-current, over-temperature, feedback loss, etc.)
Repeated frame response errors escalating to an emergency
resolution_steps: Record the error code (0x1001:00) and error register (0x1004:00).
If it's an error (non-zero code), recover by reinitialising the EtherCAT bus or restarting the system.
Interpret the 5 bytes of manufacturer-specific error data using the drive manufacturer's manual.
An emergency with error code zero is informational (the drive recovered) — just acknowledge it.
am.fb.0002.notes: Doc-grounded; note the doc itself points to the external drive manufacturer manual for the error data.

am.fb.0003.summary: An EtherCAT frame was malformed or unexpected; often transient.
likely_causes: A device failing to respond in time
resolution_steps: Check the error type (No Response, CRC, Retry Fail, etc.) for the nature of the fault.
Single spurious errors often self-recover — no action needed.
If they repeat, they usually escalate to a drive emergency; a system restart is then required.
For detail, review the logs at %amcore%/PCC/dsa.log and %amcore%/PCC/ecatmaster.log.
am.fb.0003.notes: Log paths reproduced verbatim from the doc — see _known_doc_issues (paths believed incorrect). The 'inspect cabling' advice from an earlier draft was removed because it is not in the doc.

am.fb.0004.summary: The device's firmware doesn't match the expected version and should be upgraded.
likely_causes: Device shipped/replaced with a different firmware revision
resolution_steps: Firmware upload requires the fieldbus in INIT or PREOP (not SAFEOP/OP).
Start AMCore with 'AMCore.exe -start device' to bring the fieldbus to PREOP via the Device Administrator.
Upload the firmware (interactive device-firmware-upload tool, automatic mode, or the CNCC SDK / FoE).
On success run 'AMCore.exe -start' to continue to OP; on failure run 'AMCore.exe -stop'.
Note: skipping '-start device' goes straight to OP and uploads are rejected with CNCCRESULT_INVALID_FIELDBUS_STATE.
